newsitem.title: USA: Arkansas corn, soy seedings ahead of year-ago pace.
newsitem.headline: Arkansas corn, soy seedings ahead of year-ago pace.

text.p: Soybean and corn seedings in Arkansas were ahead of the year-ago and five-year average pace during the week ended Sunday, according to the Arkansas Agricultural Statistical Service.
Below normal temperatures and wet weather prevailed across the state last week.
Soybean seedings were 13 percent complete, ahead of five percent a year ago and three percent average. Last week, soybeans were 12 percent planted.
Corn seedings were at 95 percent complete up from 90 percent a year ago and 81 percent average. That was up from the previous week at 82 percent complete.

Rice plantings were 46 percent done, above 36 percent a year ago and unchanged from the 46 percent average. Six percent of the rice had emerged, ahead of zero emerged a year ago but less than the 17 percent average pace.
Four percent of the cotton crop had been planted, the same as four percent a year ago but behind the 10 percent average.
Sorghum seedings stood at 51 percent complete, above the 36 percent of a year ago and the 39 percent average pace.
Seventy-four percent of wheat had headed, well above 27 percent a year ago and ahead of the 45 percent average pace.
